newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cargill, Ceval say Brazil takeover talk unfounded.
newsitem.headline: Cargill, Ceval say Brazil takeover talk unfounded.

text.p: The Brazilian arm of U.S. grains giant Cargill Inc and Brazilian processor Ceval Alimentos dismissed talk that Cargill had bought part or all of Ceval as unsubstantiated rumors.
Talk of the purchase drove Ceval's share price up last week to close at 14.10 reais ($13.05) Friday and the rumor spread from local stock circles to the North American cash grain trade.
Both Cargill and Ceval declined to comment on the talk Friday. But Monday, both companies dismissed the reports of a purchase as unfounded.
"Sincerely, there is absolutely nothing in it," said Paulo Prestes, spokesman for Cargill in Brazil. "It's just New York gossip."
"From the point of view of our company, there is no truth in it," added a spokesman for Ceval Alimentos.

Over the last two months, Ceval has been linked to a variety of potential buyers including Cargill, Archer Daniels Midland Co and Bunge y Born, the spokesman said. None of these rumors has been confirmed.
He denied reports that Cargill accountants had visited Ceval's offices last week. "There was nothing like that," he said.
Analysts and veteran grain traders said it would make sense for Cargill to buy Ceval, which would provide the U.S. grains firm with a solid foothold in the Brazilian soybean market.

It would also allow Cargill to counter ADM's recent purchase of Glencore Grain Holding's grain handling facilities in Brazil and Paraguay, they said. ((--Joelle Diderich, Sao Paulo newsroom +55 11 248 5417))
